definition: The level of the record: opportunity area, cluster, site or building.
The id of the record one level up, in the same file. Required for a building.
The record's name.
A narrative description of up to 400 words.
The lead body: a Planning Data organisation reference where one exists, otherwise its name.
The ONS GSS code of each council the record lies in, such as E09000009 for Ealing.
The planning authority's Planning Data organisation reference, where it differs from the council, such as development-corporation:Q20648596 for OPDC.
The name of the GLA Opportunity Area the record lies in, if any.

definition: A representative point as [longitude, latitude] in WGS84.
The area in hectares.
Whether a public authority owns the land.
The planning authority's application references for the consent or consents.
A link to the consent's documents on the planning authority's website.
Whether the record has planning permission.
The type of permission.
The date permission was granted. Displays may show the year only.
The number of homes with planning consent.
Consented floorspace in square metres, by use class.
The number of homes in the owner's vision beyond the consent. Display as a vision, not a consent.
Floorspace in the owner's vision beyond the consent, in square metres by use class. Display as a vision, not a consent.
The Ordnance Survey TOID of an existing building.
The Unique Property Reference Numbers of the addresses.
The number of storeys above ground.
The height above ground in metres.
The level of detail at which the building is modelled.
A link to a 3D model or viewer.
The names of the camera views in the 3D model that tell the location's story.
Whether the record lies in a designated opportunity or growth area.
The designations, such as a London Plan Opportunity Area.
Brownfield, greenfield or both.
How far the development has progressed.
How far the land has been brought into one ownership. Commercially sensitive: never published.
How clear the owner's vision is. Published only once the owner has seen it.
An assessment of the vision against the Local Plan. Published only once the planning authority has seen it.
An assessment of the vision against the regional plan, such as the London Plan. Published only once the planning authority has seen it.
An assessment of the vision against national policy (the NPPF). Published only once the planning authority has seen it.
The kinds of asset the location offers investors, in real estate or infrastructure.
The sectors expected to drive the location's economy.
The estimated gross value added uplift in pounds a year. Needs gva-method, gva-source and gva-date.
Whether the GVA estimate is gross or net additional.
Where the GVA estimate comes from: a link or a citation.
The date of the GVA estimate.
An investment figure in pounds. Needs value-type, value-source and value-date.
What the investment figure measures.
Where the investment figure comes from: a link or a citation.
The date of the investment figure.
How much of the development's funding is secured. Published only with the owner's agreement.
Where to send enquiries. Use a role or team address, not a personal one.
Organisations investing in the location, with an optional logo link.
The organisation that paid for the 3D model, shown as a labelled credit.
The restricted fields that the owner or planning authority has agreed may be published for this record.
The date the record came into effect.
The date the record ceased to apply, such as a site that was withdrawn.
The date the record was last checked or changed.
Where the record's facts come from: a link or a citation.
The record's licence, if it differs from the file's licence.
